title: LoomProjectQualifiedScopeAndSharedAccessRelations
clause: Enforce project-qualified graph identity and explicit cross-project shared-access relations across all Loom queries and mutations.

current_source_discovery: Inspect current project/subproject, AccessSpace, ResourceGrant, ResourceBroker and Loom identity models in stable main.
Enumerate every graph/search/backlink route and prove where project scope enters the executable query.
stop_conditions: Cross-project collaboration semantics lack an authoritative ResourceGrant/AccessSpace contract.
A query depends on UI filtering or globally unique local IDs for isolation.

scope.summary: Allow Loom to connect coding, creative, crawl, training and future tool projects without flattening their boundaries. Ordinary identity is project-qualified; cross-project visibility exists only through explicit typed shared-access relations.
forbidden_paths: Global graph scans without project predicates
Project membership as blanket cross-project access
Duplicating a shared resource into another project's authority
acceptance_criteria: Every Loom record, edge, query cursor, cache key and event carries project-qualified identity; identical local IDs in different projects never collide.
Cross-project linking uses explicit typed shared-access relations tied to ResourceGrant, AccessSpace, source scope, purpose and revocation version.
Graph, backlink, search, facet and count queries enforce scope before materialization and do not load unauthorized candidates for later UI filtering.
Shared projections preserve source ownership and cannot be edited as local copies unless an explicit domain workflow creates a new authoritative resource.
Concurrent grant revocation and context switching invalidate cursors, caches, live-query subscriptions and stale handles deterministically.
proof_targets: Run two-project same-ID collision tests against real SurrealDB.
Run same-project-private and explicit cross-project share/revoke matrices with record users.
Inspect query plans and emitted diagnostics to prove predicates precede traversal/materialization.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Authorization foundation; consumer UI MTs prove visible shared/private states.

same_project_private_resource_cases: Two members of one project see only explicitly shared private Loom resources.
cross_account_negative_cases: Forged cross-project relation or source ID fails without existence leakage.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Shared graph/search projection scope is the source-scope intersection.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Revocation invalidates cursors, subscriptions, cache entries and handles during concurrent use.
remote_saas_mcp_sync_cases: Remote collaboration ACL is mapped explicitly and never becomes a blanket local grant.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Denied degree, count, facet, label, thumbnail, timing and error class are indistinguishable from absence.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.evidence: share, deny, revoke, context-switch and traversal attribution
privacy-safe grant, cursor, cache and subscription health
crash/freeze correlation without restricted resource metadata

risk_if_missed: Handshake's many project types can collapse into one leaky graph or require unsafe duplication to reuse knowledge across projects.

risks: Project ID is added to records but omitted from one query.
Revoked data survives in a cursor or subscription.

research_provenance.selected_approach: Project-qualified graph identity plus explicit typed shared-access relations and source-scope intersection.
